verdict.rationale: WooCommerce has a first-party processor, WooPayments, and its docs cover listing transactions, viewing payouts and issuing refunds. The features page also says Woo comes bundled with the ability to accept major credit cards. However, the evidence never shows published card rates or fraud tooling, and WooPayments appears in a list of gateways to "choose from and integrate with," so whether it truly avoids wiring a gateway is only partly evidenced. Missing for 10: published card processing rates, fraud/risk tooling, independent or hands-on corroboration of WooPayments setup and payouts.

support.subject: As a merchant, I can take payments with the platform's integrated processing — published card rates, payouts, and fraud tooling — without wiring a third-party gateway

citations.quote: our Managing Money guide explains how money can flow into and out of your site. This includes topics such as listing transactions, viewing your payouts, issuing refunds to customers, and so on.
Once WooPayments is up and running, our Managing Money guide explains how money can flow into and out of your site.
Woo comes bundled with the ability to accept major credit cards, bank transfers (BACS), checks, and cash on delivery.
